definitions.explanation: Vinegar used in cooking. The polite prefix お makes this the standard everyday form; plain 酢 sounds blunt in conversation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{酢|す}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: I add a little vinegar to the dish.

examples.japanese: お{酢|す}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{健康|けんこう}→健康：02706_kenkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{飲|の}んでいる→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
examples.english: Vinegar is said to be good for your health, so I drink it every day.

notes: The polite prefix お is almost always used in everyday speech; plain ⟦{酢|す}→酢：01057_su⟧ appears mainly in compound words and technical contexts. Common collocations: お{酢|す}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧ (to put vinegar on), ⟦{酢|す}の{物|もの}→酢の物：04982_sunomono⟧ (vinegared dish), ⟦{酢飯|すめし}→酢飯：14460_sumeshi⟧ (vinegared sushi rice). Types of vinegar: ⟦{米酢|こめず}→米酢：24254_komezu⟧ (rice vinegar), ⟦{穀物酢|こくもつす}→穀物酢：24495_kokumotsusu⟧ (grain vinegar), ⟦{黒酢|くろず}→黒酢：17574_kurozu⟧ (black vinegar). Related: {酸|す}っぱい (sour — shares the same kanji root).
